title: Crab Cakes
subtitle: Pan-fried crab patties with a crisp breadcrumb crust
excerpt: The Maryland classic: crabmeat bound with just enough egg, mustard, and breadcrumbs to hold its shape, formed into patties and pan-fried until the outside is golden and the inside is hot and holding together just barely. Served with lemon and tartare sauce.

recipe.sourceNotes: Crab cakes are associated with the Chesapeake Bay region of Maryland, where blue crab has been commercially fished since the nineteenth century. The Maryland style insists on the minimum of binding material to let the crab flavour dominate: the best Maryland crab cakes use only egg, mayonnaise, a small amount of breadcrumbs, and Old Bay seasoning (a celery-seed-heavy spice blend). New England, Carolina, and other coastal American versions add more binder and flavorings. The critical technique is handling the crab mixture as little as possible to avoid breaking up the large pieces of crab meat that make the cakes satisfying. Chilling the formed patties before cooking helps them hold their shape.

content.text: Use the best quality crabmeat you can get: fresh picked crabmeat or good-quality tinned white crabmeat. Frozen crabmeat tends to be watery. Handle the mixture as little as possible when shaping; overmixing breaks up the crab lumps that give the cakes their texture. Chill for at least 30 minutes before frying so they hold together.

items.preparation: fresh or tinned white crabmeat; drained and picked of any shell
fine dry breadcrumbs; plus extra for coating
half for zest in the mix; half for serving

content.text: Pick through 400 g crabmeat to remove any pieces of shell. In a bowl, mix the egg, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, cayenne, lemon zest, parsley, and spring onion. Add the crabmeat and breadcrumbs and fold gently together using the minimum mixing. The mixture should barely hold; if too wet, add a little more breadcrumb.
Divide into 8 portions and shape into patties about 2 cm thick. Press the outside lightly in extra breadcrumbs. Place on a baking tray and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Heat the butter and oil in a large, non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the crab cakes in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and heated through. Do not move them until they release cleanly from the pan. Serve with lemon wedges and tartare sauce.
